picks.headline: Google's quantum computer learns from its own errors mid-computation
picks.excerpt: Google researchers built a reinforcement-learning system that lets a quantum computer learn from its own error-correction data and recalibrate itself mid-computation. The approach cut logical error rates about 20% beyond conventional calibration and stayed 3.5x more stable under hardware drift on the Willow processor, pointing toward autonomously self-tuning quantum machines.
picks.rationale: Novel, credible result (Google/Willow) where RL turns error-correction data into live self-recalibration — a concrete method advance, distinct from every published science card and never previously covered.
